name: Six-month delayed nerve repair in a large animal, with and without distal-pathway support

design.model: proximal hindlimb nerve transection, repair delayed six months
design.intervention: an intervention intended to maintain Schwann cell support (for example chronic low-frequency stimulation of the distal segment)
design.comparator: immediate repair; delayed repair without intervention
design.readout: muscle force, motor endplate counts, motor unit number estimation, Schwann cell phenotype at repair

discriminates: If delayed-plus-intervention approaches immediate repair on force, the window is a pathway problem and can be extended; if it matches untreated delay, the muscle is the limit and the map should say so.

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (Crossref/Europe PMC), checked 2026-09-14; no source opened at figure level
